threads.title: The parable of the rich fool — laying up treasure for self, not rich toward Elohim
threads.summary_md: Luke alone carries this parable. A man in the crowd asks the King to settle an inheritance dispute; the King answers with the warning — *Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth* (Luke 12:15) — and then the parable: the rich man whose ground brought forth plentifully, who pulls down his barns to build greater, who says to his soul *Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* (Luke 12:19), and to whom Elohim (God) says *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). The verdict — *So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God)* (Luke 12:21) — pairs with the broader treasure-in-heaven catena of Matthew 6 / Luke 12:33-34. Framework-substance: the rich-fool is the wisdom-stream's standing target (Qohelet/Ecclesiastes 2's *I made me great works* register, Tehillim 49's *they that trust in their wealth*, Sirach 11:18-19's near-identical parable). The post-harvest sifting tests fruit, and *much goods laid up* is not fruit.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *A man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.* The Qohelet (Ecclesiastes) 5:10 substance — *He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.*

*Take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* The Qohelet (Ecclesiastes) 8:15 surface-formula *a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry* — Qohelet's own bracketing question the rich fool collapses into a closed answer. The rich fool reads Qohelet's *under the sun* register and forgets the *fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments* that closes the book.

*Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee.* Iyov (Job) 27:8 — *For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when Eloah (God) taketh away his soul?* The same architecture: the gain accumulated, the soul taken, the gain unused.

The rich fool is the Tehillim (Psalm) 49 type — *They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches; none of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him.*

*Then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* The Tehillim (Psalm) 49:17 answer — *For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him.* The barns get pulled down; the soul gets required; the goods get inherited by someone else.

*So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God).* The verdict ties straight into the Matthew 6:19-21 *lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth... but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven* — and into Luke 12:33-34 the very next pericope where the King names the same substance.

Luke's own internal parallel — *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not.* The rich-fool is the negative example; vv.33-34 is the positive instruction. The two pericopes are one substance.

threads.title: The rich fool who knows not his time in Sirach
threads.summary_md: Luke 12:16-21's parable of the rich fool — the man whose ground brought forth plentifully, who pulls down his barns to build greater, and who says to his soul *Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* — walks an architecture the Hebrew library's wisdom-stream had already named word-for-word. Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:18 names the hollow reward of the hoarder: *there is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* Sirach 11:19 lands the verdict the parable lands: *whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.* The two things the rich fool does not reckon with — *he knoweth not what time shall come upon him,* and *he must leave those things to others, and die* — are exactly the two things Luke 12:20 names: *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* The wisdom-stream named the rich fool centuries before the King spoke the parable; the gospel walks the same architecture and seals it with the verdict — *so is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God)* (Luke 12:21).

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 11:19 — *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods.* Sirach's rich man speaks the rich fool's line of Luke 12:19 centuries early.
Ecclesiasticus 11:18 — *waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* The hoarder's whole reward is the heap left behind when the soul is required at Luke 12:20.

threads.title: Treasure in the heavens laid up by alms in Tobit and Sirach
threads.summary_md: Luke 12:33-34's sell-and-give-alms teaching — *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also* — walks an architecture the Hebrew library had already named at the verse-level. Tobit 4:9 names the laid-up-treasure-against-the-day teaching directly: *for you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit 4:10 names the protection-economy: *because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:11 names the lay-up-treasure-by-the-commandments architecture: *lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* Sirach 29:12 names the storehouse-of-alms protection: *shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* The Hebrew library uses the same *lay up* and *storehouse* and *treasure against the day* images the gospel walks; the gospel names the heaven-bag that faileth not, where no thief approaches and no moth corrupts — the treasure the open hand of the alms-giver lays up where loss cannot reach.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: Tobit 4:9 — *a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The alms given now are the bags that wax not old, the treasure that faileth not (Luke 12:33).
Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The open hand delivers from death; its treasure is in the heavens where no thief approacheth (Luke 12:33).

Ecclesiasticus 29:11 — *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High.* The commandment keeper's treasure is the *treasure in the heavens that faileth not* of Luke 12:33, laid up by alms.

Sirach 29:12 — *shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* The Hebrew library's *storehouse* image; Luke 12:33-34's *treasure in the heavens... for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also* walks the same storehouse-of-treasure architecture at the heavenly level.

threads.title: Names written before the Great One and not blotted out — 1 Enoch 103–104 and confessing or denying him
threads.summary_md: *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). *But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:33). The confessing he promises is a name spoken before the Father, and the library knows the names are already written there. Enoch swears to the righteous what he has read: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). And a few lines on: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Names are written before, and the only thing scripture ever says can happen to a written name is that it is blotted out, at Sinai when Moses pleads, in David's psalm, and in the promise to Sardis: *He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5). Confess his name before the Father is the same phrase Matthew 10 uses. The one who lives out the confession keeps a name that was always there; the one who denies him under pressure is risking the blotting, which is why the warning is spoken to those whose names are written and not to anyone else.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of Adam also confess before the angels of Elohim (God): But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of Elohim (God).* The confess-or-deny architecture tied to the books-of-life.

threads.title: Binding the strong man — the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Isaiah 49; Ezekiel 36; 1 Enoch 15; Proverbs 18)
threads.summary_md: When the Pharisees call his work the work of Beelzebub, Yahusha shows whose power is truly at work. *How can one enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man?* — this is Isaiah's promise: *Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith Yahuah (LORD)... I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children* (Isaiah 49:24-25). To plunder the strong man's house is to take back the captives from the mighty. And by what Spirit? *I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27) — the Spirit of Elohim by which the devils are cast out is the same Spirit that writes the Torah on the heart; the kingdom come is a people made to keep the commandments, not freed from them. The library even tells us what these unclean spirits ARE: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."* (1 Enoch 16:1) — the spirits of the dead giants, offspring of the Watchers, the very devils the Son binds. To call this work satanic is the unpardonable sin — *if a man sin against Yahuah (LORD), who shall intreat for him?* (1 Samuel 2:25). For the mouth betrays the heart: *Death and life are in the power of the tongue* (Proverbs 18:21); *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.*

threads.title: Beware the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees — the doctrine that works through the whole (Exodus 12:15; 1 Corinthians 5:6)
threads.summary_md: *Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees* (16:6). The disciples think he speaks of bread; he means *the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees* (16:12). The figure is drawn straight from the feast: *Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread... that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 12:15) — leaven is the small thing purged out, the thing that secretly works through the whole. Hosea already turned that figure on a corrupt heart: *They are all adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker, who ceaseth from raising after he hath kneaded the dough, until it be leavened* (Hosea 7:4). And Sha'ul keeps the same Passover-grammar exactly: *Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?* (1 Corinthians 5:6) — *Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth* (1 Corinthians 5:8). The feast is kept; the leaven to be put away is false doctrine and malice — exactly the leaven Yahusha names.

threads.title: The faithful and wise servant and the day of visitation — Sirach 11, 16, 27 + Wisdom of Solomon 3
threads.summary_md: Matt 24:45-51's faithful-and-wise-servant vs evil-servant substance — the substantial-stewardship-substance the King walks against the substantial-inherited-Reformation-eternal-security-substance — read against the wisdom-stream's articulation of the reward-according-to-works + post-harvest-sifting + day-of-visitation architecture in Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) and Wisdom of Solomon. Four moves: Sirach 11:26 names the direct verbal-anchor for the reward-according-to-his-ways substance (*for it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways*) the substantial-faithful-and-wise-servant walks-into at Matt 24:46; Sirach 16:14 names the every-man-shall-find-according-to-his-works substance the substantial-greater-stewardship-substance at Matt 24:47 walks-the-architecture-of (*make him ruler over all his goods*); Sirach 27:4 names the substantial-post-harvest-sifting architecture (*as when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains*) the substantial-evil-servant at Matt 24:51 walks-the-judgment-substance of — the substance the prophet-Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) walked at Ezekiel 18:24 (*when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness... all his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned*) — ties-back to the substantial Matthew 23 seven-woes-against-the-hypocrites the evil-servant walks-the-same-substance-as the substantial-Pharisaic-Sadducean-leadership had-walked; Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 names the time-of-visitation substance (*in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble*) the substantial-faithful-and-wise-servant at Matt 24:46 walks-the-shining-substance-of in continuity with Daniel 12:3 + Matthew 13:43. The framework reads the cluster against the substantial-inherited-Reformation-eternal-security-substance — the substantial-substance is not the substantial-one-time-confession-substance but the substantial-walking-out-of-the-substantial-works the substantial-Spirit-internalized-Torah-substance walks per the substantial-new-heart-of-Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27, the substantial-grace as the substantial-door-home opened-by-the-substantial-categorically-exempt-One's-voluntary-walking-into-the-shameful-death the substantial-categorically-bound owed, with the substantial-consequences-of-walking-off-the-substantial-Way still-real because the substantial-Way is-real per *Grace, the Way, the New Heart, and the Mercy of Depart*.

threads.title: The few saved, the many lost, and the post-harvest sifting — 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7 and 8's articulation of the world-to-come-for-few + the work-shall-follow + the judgment-seat-of-the-Most-High
threads.summary_md: Matt 25's three sifting-parables — the ten-virgins shut-door at vv.10-13, the unprofitable-servant cast-into-outer-darkness at v.30, and the sheep-and-goats-judgment at vv.31-46 — read against the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the post-harvest-sifting per Red Line #11 in 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7 and 8. Four moves: 2 Esdras 8:1 names THE direct verbal-anchor for the world-to-come-for-few substance (*The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few*) — the substantial-architecture the shut-door at Matt 25:10 walks; 2 Esdras 8:3 names the direct articulation of the many-created-but-few-saved substance (*There be many created, but few shall be saved*) — the operative-substance of the substantial-many-called-but-few-chosen at Matt 22:14 and the substantial *I know you not* at Matt 25:12; 2 Esdras 7:35 names the work-shall-follow + the reward-shall-be-shewed substance — the substantial-substance the unprofitable-servant walks-into at Matt 25:30's outer-darkness; 2 Esdras 7:33 names the Most-High-on-the-seat-of-judgment substance — the substantial-Davidic-Messianic-throne-of-his-glory the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) sits-upon at Matt 25:32 + the gathering-of-all-nations + the separation-substance the prophet-Yo'el (Joel) walked at Joel 3:1-14 walks-into. The framework reads the cluster as the wisdom-stream's direct corroboration of the post-harvest-sifting per Red Line #11 — the substantial-wheat-after-the-gathering is sifted-into-wheat-and-chaff; the substantial-foolish-virgins and the substantial-unprofitable-servant are wheat-that-did-not-bear-the-fruit-of-readiness-or-stewardship, NOT tares (the substantial-tares were burned at the harvest of Matt 13's wheat-and-tares + Matt 24's eagles-to-the-carcase). The substantial-name-can-be-substantively-blotted-out-of-the-Book-of-Life per Exodus 32:33 + Psalm 69:28 + Revelation 3:5 — the substantial-warning is-given-to-the-substantial-wheat, NOT to the substantial-tares. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the few-saved-many-lost + the work-shall-follow + the judgment-seat-of-the-Most-High architecture.

threads.title: The diligent stewardship versus the slothful servant — Sirach's wisdom-stream articulation of the trade-the-deposit substance for the parable of the talents
threads.summary_md: Matt 25:14-30's parable-of-the-talents — the substantial-substance of the present-age-stewardship between the Ascension and the second-coming + the two-faithful-servants both rewarded equally on faithfulness (NOT on quantity) + the unprofitable-servant cast-into-outer-darkness for-the-substantial-failure-of-stewardship — read against the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the diligent-labour-versus-the-slothful substance in Sirach (Ecclesiasticus). Four moves: Sirach 11:21 names the trust-and-abide-in-your-labour substance (*Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour*) — the substantial-substance the faithful-servants walk-out at the doubling of the talents; Sirach 22:1 names THE direct verbal-anchor for the slothful-substance (*A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone*) — the operative-form of the substantial-failure-of-action the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-against at the unprofitable-servant; Sirach 33:28 names the master's set-him-to-work substance with the substantial-consequences-for-the-failure-of-the-work; Sirach 51:30 names THE direct verbal-anchor for the work-your-work-betimes + the reward-in-his-time substance (*Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward*) — the substantial-reward the substantial-faithful-servants walk-into is the substantial-millennial-reign-stewardship per Revelation 2:26-27, 3:21, 5:10, 20:4-6 + the twelve-thrones at Matt 19:28 + the marriage-of-the-Lamb at Revelation 19:7-9. The framework reads the cluster as the wisdom-stream's direct corroboration of the post-harvest-sifting per Red Line #11's architecture — the unprofitable-servant has-been-given-the-talent (the substantial-grace) + has-been-named-as-a-servant (the substantial-relationship) + has-been-cast-into-outer-darkness for-the-substantial-failure-of-stewardship (the substantial-loss); the substantial-Reformation-eternal-security-substance is explicitly-ruled-out — the grace and the opportunity and the loss are all-three-substantial at-the-same-substance per Red Line #10's sola-fide-grammar-corrected-by-the-completed-sentence framework. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture at the diligence-and-slothfulness-substance; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks the operative-form at the parable of the talents.

threads.title: A man's foes shall be they of his own household — the family torn in the day of destruction
threads.summary_md: *Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.* (Matthew 10:34-36). He is quoting Micah, and Micah is describing a day. Enoch describes the same day, and the house is where it tears first: *And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children, And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them: Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them, And shall have no pity on their beloved ones.* (1 Enoch 99:5). Then the blood: *And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten And brothers one with another shall fall in death Till the streams flow with their blood. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons’ sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another.* (1 Enoch 100:1-2). The enmity set in the garden between the two seeds does not stop at the front door. Wheat and tares can be born under one roof, and when the Shepherd's voice is heard by one and not the other, the line runs straight through the family. What the King warns his disciples of in this age is the first showing of the division Enoch saw finished in the day of destruction, when the house that would not hear falls on itself.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *I am come to send fire on the earth... Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division.* Same family-division architecture as Matthew 10:34-36; the seed-war runs at the family-level.

threads.title: No forgiveness for the hardened heart — Jubilees 15, 1 Enoch 65, Wisdom of Solomon 12
threads.summary_md: *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). The men he says this to have just watched the Spirit cast out a demon and called it the work of Beelzebub. They saw the thing clearly and named it the devil's, and that is the hardening the library already knew had no road back from it. Enoch was told it about the ones who had learned the Watchers' secrets and would not turn: *And these—they have no place of repentance for ever, because they have shown them what was hidden, and they are the damned: but as for thee, my son, Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits knows that thou art pure, and guiltless of this reproach concerning the secrets.* (1 Enoch 65:11). Jubilees names the same wrath for the ones who set the covenant aside on purpose: *there will be great wrath from Yahuah (the Lord) ... because they have forsaken His covenant and have turned aside from His word* (Jubilees 15:33-34). And the Wisdom of Solomon says why the patience ran out on the Canaanites: he gave them place for repentance, not being ignorant that their malice was bred in them and that their way of thinking would never change (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). None of these is about a slip of the tongue. They are about a settled refusal, eyes open, that has made up its mind against the correction. That is why the one who fears he has committed this sin almost certainly has not; the fear is a conscience still working, and a hardened heart does not lie awake over it.

threads.title: Post-harvest sifting
threads.summary_md:
The wilderness of the peoples — Ezekiel 20:33–44 — is the Tanakh source for the sheep-and-goats separation, 'depart from me, I never knew you,' and the weeping-and-gnashing-of-teeth passages.

Yahuah (the LORD) gathers the scattered house out of all nations, brings them face to face in the wilderness, causes them to pass under the rod, and purges out the rebels from among them. The 'depart from me, ye cursed' of Matthew 25:41 is the 'they shall not enter into the land of Yashar'el (Israel)' of Ezekiel 20:38. The weeping and gnashing of teeth is the loathing of self in Ezekiel 20:43 — 'ye shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for all your evils that ye have committed.'

The gospel passages are not eternal-hell prooftexts spoken to unbelievers. They are the post-harvest sifting of the gathered wheat. The sheep are the fruitful within the covenant body; the goats are the unfruitful within the covenant body. 'I never knew you' is spoken to those who prophesied in his name, cast out devils in his name, did many wonderful works in his name (Matthew 7:22) — not to tares. Names get blotted out in this sifting; no name is added.

And the same chapter that names the sifting names the mercy: 'I have wrought with you for my name's sake, not according to your wicked ways' (Ezekiel 20:44). The hang-the-head and the name's-sake grace are the same verse pair.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: The discerning-the-time / reconciling-with-the-adversary register — the framework's substance of recognizing the appointed-hour while it is still being walked toward. The wheat that does not discern is the unfruitful-wheat the warning falls on.

threads.title: The righteous in the Father's hand — Wisdom of Solomon and Sirach
threads.summary_md: Matt 6:25-34's take-no-thought / seek-first-the-kingdom teaching grounds the kingdom-citizens trust-economy in the Father's standing care for the righteous. The Hebrew library's Wisdom of Solomon and Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) name the architecture directly. Wisdom 5:15 names the care-of-the-righteous-is-with-the-Most-High register: *the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* Wisdom 5:16 names the glorious-kingdom-from-the-Father's-hand + right-hand-covering protection-economy: *therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* Sirach 11:14 names the all-comes-of-Yahuah architecture: *prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).* The Father is the source of both prosperity and adversity; the kingdom-citizens orientation carries through both because the Father administers both. The gospel's seek-first teaching walks the same Hebrew library architecture: the kingdom received from the Father's hand carries the daily-provision the seeker does not have to anxiously grasp for.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: The consider-the-lilies / consider-the-ravens architecture — same substance as Matthew 6:25-34 with the Lukan addition of *Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom* (Luke 12:32).

threads.title: Treasures laid up by the open hand in Tobit and Sirach
threads.summary_md: Matt 6:19-21's treasures-in-heaven teaching — *lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth ... but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal* — walks an architecture the Hebrew library had already named at the verse-level. Tobit 4:9 names the laid-up-treasure-against-the-day-of-necessity teaching directly: *for you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit 4:10 names the protection-economy: *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:11 names the lay-up-treasure-by-the-commandments architecture: *lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* Sirach 29:12 names the storehouse-of-alms protection: *shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* The Hebrew library uses the same *lay up* and *storehouse* images the gospel walks; the gospel names the corruption-proof storehouse the open hand fills.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *Provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not... For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.* The treasure-in-heaven substance — same architecture as Matthew 6:19-21 and the Tobit / Sirach wisdom-stream witness.
